title: SPDCN: Strip-based Deformable Convolutional Network for Steel Surface Defect Segmentation
mechanism: Deformable convolution whose offsets come from decoupled horizontal and vertical strip convolutions, so the sampling grid aligns with elongated, anisotropic defects.
adaptation: Gridline (IoU 0.283, recall 0.33) and splice (never predicted) are axis-aligned in rectified cells, and rot90 augmentation keeps them axis-aligned. Use strip-offset deformable blocks in the U-Net++ decoder with the 24-class head.
min_experiment: SPDCN-style decoder blocks vs house. Metrics: gridline IoU and recall, plus mIoU_rob on test and module-grouped 5-fold CV; crack IoU as a guard. Kill if gridline CV IoU gains < 0.03.
evidence: R: 89.60 mIoU on NEU-Seg with 3.54M params (abstract). The author page github.com/DWlzm is named; the repository itself is unverified.

alt_notes.adaptation: Closest domain here: grey industrial surfaces with cracks and scratches. Insert ADADC blocks at 1/2 and 1/4 resolution in the U-Net++ decoder; 1-ch, 24 classes.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: ADADC decoder, 5 seeds; baseline house. Metrics: crack relF1@2, components found, gridline IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill: all gains < 0.01 and E1 < +0.02.

alt_notes.adaptation: Cells are axis-aligned, so strips fit gridline fingers (IoU 0.283, recall 0.33), busbars, ribbons, splice; learned offsets cover diagonal cracks. Replace 3x3 convs in the last two U-Net++ decoder stages, keep the ImageNet encoder.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house with ADADC in last two decoder stages; baseline: house; metric: CV gridline IoU and crack relF1@2; kill if gridline IoU gain < +0.03 and crack n.d.
